name: Planning Commission Adjourned Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, MAY 21, 2024

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:02 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Nicklas, Romanelli, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MAY 5, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 5, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

NONE

7.  PUBLIC HEARING

NONE

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240164; LOCATION: 3410 Tanglewood Lane, Rolling
  Hills States, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Carol Beth Cozen; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-240165) for a project that includes a 77 square foot (SF)
  second story addition, a 224 SF first story addition, a 584 SF proposed deck to the first
  story, and interior remodel to an existing split-level residence.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation on Planning Application No. PA-240164
summarizing the staff report. Staff determined that this project meets all of the required
Neighborhood Compatibility findings.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-240164 (NC-240165) with the conditions outlined in the staff report.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if staff received any comments from the neighbors. Assistant
Planner Kawagoe stated that no comments were received by staff.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired about staging for construction. Assistant Planner
Kawagoe stated that this can be added to the conditions of approval.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  1
   APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240164 WITH THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: MEDAWAR, NICKLAS, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER
NOES
ABSENT: OLSON, REPP-LOADSMAN, YOO
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240164, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240165) at 3410
Tanglewood Lane. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City
Council, by its own motion may appeal this project.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE; Staff is seeking direction and input from the Planning
  Commission on the proposed draft Chapter 17.28 - Commercial Limited Mixed-Use District
  and Chapter 17.30 - Commercial General Mixed-Use District standards.

Community Development Director Naughton provided an overview of the overall implementation
efforts of the City’s General Plan, which was adopted by the City Council in 2022. This includes
adopting the zoning map to be in compliance with the general plan and two proposed districts,
which are the Commercial General Mixed-Use and the Commercial Limited Mixed-Use Districts.
Director Naughton further explained the new zoning overlays and zoning designations.

Director Naughton asked that Commission about the following special development standards:

  1. Arcades – should a locational standard for an arcade be restricted to more than 500 feet
  from a school be added to the zoning code.
  2. Day nurseries, daycare centers – should a requirement to identify and provide loading and
  unloading spaces be added to the zoning code, and should adult day care centers be also
  be required to provide loading and unloading spaces.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS commented that drop-off or pick-up for day care centers has been
previously discussed and stated that it should be added for safety concerns.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about the arcades. Director Naughton stated that she
could not find the historic context for why arcades were prohibited by the city’s code. and also
stated that this item came up due to this same reason. The previously approved bowling alley at
the Promenade is aware that this was coming before the commission, and they will be applying
for a Conditional Use Permit if the Planning Commission and City Council adopts that this use is
permitted by CUP.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about the 500’ within a residential district and asked if
this also applies to residential districts in other cities. Director Naughton stated that there are very
few residential properties that border single family residential in Rolling Hills Estates and added
that when writing these development standards, she had RPV single-family residential in mind.
She added that the code applies to properties within the City; however, when notices are mailed,
they include properties in other cities which may be within a 500’ radius.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if the arcade hours could be restricted during school hours. Director
Naughton stated that the operational hours could be restricted; however, restricting a portion of a
business’ uses may be difficult to regulate.

A brief discussion ensued.

The Planning Commission agreed to allow arcades with a CUP.

The Planning Commission agreed to keep the operational hours requirement for day care centers
and remove the other requirements.

Director Naughton stated that restaurants that are less than 5,000 SF, with beer and wine license
only close by midnight and are allowed by right. For the Commercial General Mixed-Use, the
same conditions apply; however, if the space is larger than 5,000 SF, then it will go through the
administrative review process. Grocery and food markets that are greater than 10,000 square feet
would also go through the administrative review process.

Director Naughton added that restaurants with full alcohol licenses, noise, or odor inducing type
uses like char broilers or BBQ smokers would be required to go through the CUP process. She

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 21, 2024
  2
 also added that parking requirements were modified to more reasonable standards in order to
encourage more restaurants to come into the City.

Director Naughton provided an overview of the development standards in the Commercial
General Mixed-Use district and stated that the minimum setback in front of a building to the public
right-of-way is 5’ and the proposed maximum building height is 50’.

A discussion ensued on the development standards.

The Planning Commission agreed that the height maximum should be set at 50’ and agreed with
the minimum setback of 5’.

Director Naughton stated that the residential development standards for the Commercial General
Mixed-Use District are 30 dwelling units/acre and the same general standards; staff is in the
process of creating objective design standards. The required open space is 300 SF/unit.

Director Naughton stated that there are two sites that will have the Commercial Limited Mixed-
Use designation. They are at Highridge Road at Armada Spring Springs Road, and Rolling Hills
Road at Palos Verdes Drive North (Kelly’s Korner).

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if hotels and motels are defined in the code. Director
Naughton stated that if they are not, the definitions will be added to the code.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, the code will be amended and
restated and, in some cases, entire sections will be removed since they are no longer used.

Director Naughton explained the current development standards for Commercial Limited. The lot
coverage is currently 25% and 30% is required to be landscaped and stated that this will be
reviewed and a more reasonable percentage will be proposed by staff.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS expressed his concern with the changes to the Commercial Limited
Mixed-Use designation. Director Naughton explained that these changes are being proposed in
order to implement what was approved in the general plan.

A discussion ensued on the lot coverage percentage.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI directed that staff determine an appropriate lot coverage
percentage giving consideration that these sites back up to residential districts.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the required RHNA (Regional Housing Needs
Allocation) number for the City. Director Naughton stated that it is 191 units and within this number
there are levels of affordable housing that need to be met. Director Naughton further explained
how this number is met.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS expressed concern with the number of units that are being allowed
for. Director Naughton explained that the General Plan is directing the changes that are being
proposed to be implemented.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton explained that the
Workforce Housing Overlay Zone is also being directed by the General Plan. There are school
sites and a church site that has been designated, more so for their available space, for workforce
housing. A Conditional Use Permit would be required if there was a proposal for this type of
housing project.

In a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton provided a brief overview
about the overlays that are being changed or added.

Director Naughton stated that at the next meeting these changes will be presented in ordinance
form for the Planning Commission to review and a recommendation is made to present the
ordinance to the City Council; it will be presented at its second meeting in June.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated the there is a concern with an ADU under construction
that backs up to Ernie Howlett Park. Director Naughton stated that staff will look into it.

CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he has been approached by the tenants along Bart Earl Way and
stated that there is a concern with the retaining wall. He stated that there are issues with his

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 21, 2024
  3
 building in regard to drainage; and contractors have told him that work cannot be done until the
retaining wall is fixed. Director Naughton stated that this may be a civil issue, but the staff can go
out and see if there is a safety concern.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MAY 14, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 8:52 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting on Monday, June 3 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Medawar, Chair
